papers.title: Multi-scale vision transformer model with UAV-based hyperspectral imagery for early identification of pine wilt disease infected trees
papers.authors: Hao Shi, Ruirui Zhang, Meixiang Chen, Huixiang Liu, Danzhu Zhang
papers.abstract: Pine Wilt Disease (PWD), caused by the pine wood nematode ( Bursaphelenchus xylophilus ), is a devastating forest disease characterized by rapid spread and high mortality. During its pathogenesis, the green attack and early stage are critical for disease control. However, RGB UAV images lack obvious visual features at these stages, which limits the accuracy of existing identification methods. This study aims to develop a Multi-Scale Vision Transformer Model specifically designed for UAV hyperspectral data. The primary objectives are to improve the identification capability for the green attack and early stages of PWD. To accurately capture subtle changes in the spectral and spatial features of pine trees during the green attack stage, an efficient spectral-spatial feature fusion module was designed. Meanwhile, an improved Gaussian self-attention mechanism was introduced to enhance the modeling of spectral differences between central pixels and their neighboring pixels. papers.title: Climate-Based Modeling of Invasive Species Impact on Urban Green Infrastructure Using CLIMEX and Remote Sensing Data
papers.authors: A. Suresh kumar, C. Rajan
papers.source: OpenAlex / Journal of Smart Infrastructure and Environmental Sustainability
papers.abstract: The pace at which invasive alien species are established and spread is becoming a threat, especially to urban ecosystems, due, in part, to the variability of climates, urban growth, and fragmentation of habitats. These biological invasions are highly dangerous to urban green infrastructure (UGI), which sabotages biodiversity, ecological services, and ecological resilience in the long term. A unravelled modelling approach to employ the CLIMEX model of species distribution as well as the spatial analysis of ecosystems via remote sensing to observe invasion risk zones and map them in the fast urbanising landscapes was created in this work. The climatic suitability of chosen invasive species in the current and future climate conditions under parameters serving as temperature, precipitation, and humidity was simulated with the help of the CLIMEX model, and the land cover dynamics and vegetation indices (as well as the urban heat islands) were measured with the assistance of remote sensing data (Sentinel-2 and ModiS) measurements. papers.title: Chemical Ecology and Management of Imported Fire Ants
papers.authors: Jian Chen
papers.abstract: Imported fire ants ( Solenopsis invicta and S. richteri ) are invasive pests that were introduced into the United States via Mobile, Alabama, in the early twentieth century. As these species spread, interbreeding led to the emergence of hybrid populations. Their rapid expansion and ecological dominance prompted extensive control efforts, including chemical eradication campaigns and biologically informed strategies. Today, fire ants infest over 140 million hectares across the southern United States, affecting public health, agriculture, and ecosystems. Despite decades of research, many fire ant semiochemicals remain unidentified because of the ants’ complex social behavior and because multicomponent chemical signals occur in trace amounts and are difficult to isolate, especially those involved in aerial mating. Additionally, components often lack activity unless presented in specific combinations. These challenges limit traditional bioassay-guided structure elucidation. This review summarizes advances in fire ant chemical ecology, highlights persistent knowledge gaps, and proposes innovative strategies to accelerate pheromone discovery and improve management.

papers.title: Aggregation pattern, economic injury level, and sampling protocol for Chaetanaphothrips orchidii (Thysanoptera: Thripidae) in citrus orchards
papers.authors: Carolina Juncá‐Morales, José Catalán, Jesica Pérez‐Rodríguez, César Monzó, Alejandro Tena
papers.abstract: Abstract Chaetanaphothrips orchidii (Moulton) is an invasive citrus pest in the Mediterranean, which has damaged up to 70% of fruit production. In this study, we aim to calculate its aggregation pattern, develop a sampling plan, and determine its economic injury levels (EIL). For these aims, 10 citrus orchards from Eastern Spain were sampled twice per month between 2018 and 2020, with sampling years varying among orchards. Both larvae and adults of C. orchidii tended to aggregate in fruits in contact with other fruits or leaves, in most orchards and years sampled. Fruit damage percentage increased with thrips occupation during the year. To monitor C. orchidii in citrus, we recommend sampling fruits in contact twice per month from June to October with either enumerative or binomial sampling. The manuscript provides an EIL calculator that considers management cost and revenue specific to each orchard. This tool estimated an EIL of 4.45% of fruit occupied by C. orchidii, for a standard Navel orange orchard sprayed with the maximum allowed concentration of acetamiprid. papers.title: When nematodes take flight: Multi-scale dispersal of the beech leaf disease nematode in forest ecosystems
papers.authors: Erika Consoli, Lily Berry, Niclas Lyndby, Miriam R. Wayman, Lucas W. DeGroote
papers.abstract: Beech leaf disease, caused by the invasive foliar nematode Litylenchus crenatae, is an emerging threat to Fagus grandifolia across North America. Since its initial detection in 2012, the disease has spread to a total of 16 U.S. states and the Canadian Province of Ontario; however, the mechanisms underlying nematode dispersal remain poorly understood. This study evaluated multiple potential dispersal pathways across two forest sites in central Pennsylvania through integrated field surveys, environmental monitoring, and experimental validation. Weekly sampling was conducted to characterize nematode population dynamics in relation to temperature, precipitation, wind, and humidity. Long distance water-mediated dispersal was assessed through creek sampling, while biotic dispersal was investigated through field sampling from migratory bird feet during high-moisture events and a controlled greenhouse transmission experiment. Wind dispersal was further examined in a pilot study using unmanned aerial vehicle-assisted rainwater collection during precipitation events. papers.title: Prevention of Destructive Fishing in the Waters of Tual City: Effective Surveillance and Law Enforcement Strategies
papers.authors: Suharta ., Sigit Bintoro, Riyan Maulana, Ismi Isti Anah
papers.source: Crossref / International Journal of Multidisciplinary Research and Growth Evaluation
papers.abstract: <jats:p>Destructive fishing in the waters of Tual City remains a significant environmental and socio-economic issue, threatening marine biodiversity and the livelihoods of local fishermen. This study analyzes the problem using a SWOT approach, identifying strengths such as existing government regulations and rich marine resources, weaknesses including limited enforcement capacity and economic dependence on harmful fishing practices, opportunities such as growing global demand for sustainable seafood, and threats like illegal fishing and climate change. Based on the SWOT analysis, several policy recommendations are proposed, including strengthening law enforcement, promoting sustainable alternative livelihoods, enhancing education and awareness programs, expanding marine protected areas (MPAs), and creating market incentives for responsible fisheries. These strategies aim to transition Tual City towards sustainable fisheries management, balancing environmental conservation with economic development. Effective implementation of these policies will not only mitigate destructive fishing but also ensure long-term resilience for both the ecosystem and local fishing communities.</jats:p>

papers.title: Bayesian neural network for plant disease detection: A role of prior knowledge in data-scarce agricultural systems
papers.authors: A Tharshiniremila, R Vasanthi, R. Pangayar Selvi, M Kalpana, Chandrasekaran Indu Rani
papers.abstract: Plant diseases are a major threat to global food security, causing an estimated annual economic loss of approximately USD 220 billion. Even though deep learning models excel at image-based disease detection, the requirement for many labelled images with a quantitative prediction uncertainty can be problematic in real-world agricultural applications. Bayesian neural networks (BNNs) overcome these limitations by incorporating prior knowledge from plant pathology, symptom morphology and environmental factors within a probabilistic learning framework. This approach not only improves prediction accuracy but also yields calibrated uncertainty estimates alongside each prediction. This review synthesises recent studies on BNNs, focusing on domain-knowledge, data-driven and functional priors for plant disease detection. The evidence gained from the studies reviewed indicates that BNNs consistently outperform deterministic models, especially in low-data regimes, as may be the case for smallholder farming characterised by heterogeneous environments and limited annotation resources. papers.title: Arthropods communities in organic orchards and adjacent hedgerows on Terceira Island (Azores, Portugal): a dataset supporting biological control research
papers.authors: Sophie Wallon, António Domingues, Alejandra Ros‐Prieto, Sébastien Lhoumeau, David João Horta Lopes
papers.abstract: Organic orchards and their associated hedgerows can function as important ecological infrastructures in agricultural landscapes by providing shelter, alternative prey, floral resources and overwintering sites for arthropods involved in natural pest regulation. This role is particularly relevant on oceanic islands, where agricultural mosaics include endemic, native non-endemic and introduced taxa, and where biodiversity-friendly production systems may contribute to both ecosystem-service provisioning and early detection of potentially invasive species. Under the scope of the BIODIVERSA+ COMCHA project, we sampled arthropod assemblages in six orchards certified under the Organic Production System on Terceira Island, Azores, Portugal, comparing the orchard interior with adjacent hedgerows. Sampling was carried out in September 2025 and May 2026 using standardised active methods: SLAM traps (Sea, Land and Air Malaise), nocturnal Active Aerial Search, nocturnal foliage beating and diurnal foliage beating. papers.title: Toward evidence-based fish welfare regulation: policy lessons from Chile, Norway, and Scotland
papers.authors: Juan Antonio Valdés
papers.abstract: Aquaculture has become a major contributor to global food production, but its rapid expansion and intensification have increased concerns regarding the welfare of farmed fish. Although advances in welfare science have generated animal-based measures, operational welfare indicators, and increasingly sophisticated monitoring technologies, their incorporation into regulatory frameworks remains uneven. This review examines the evolution of fish welfare regulation and compares the regulatory approaches of Chile, Norway, and Scotland, three major salmon-producing jurisdictions representing distinct models of welfare governance. The analysis distinguishes between legislation that directly establishes welfare obligations and sanitary, environmental, biosecurity, and production regulations that indirectly influence welfare determinants. Chile combines explicit legal recognition of fish welfare with an extensive sanitary and environmental regulatory architecture, although standardized animal-based welfare assessment, intervention criteria, and welfare-specific auditing remain limited. Methods: In June 2016, a total of 30 toxic element samples were taken from surface soils to examine their contents of lead (Pb), Zinc (Zn), Copper (Cu), Nickel (Ni), Arsenic (As), Chromium (Cr), and Cadmium (Cd). papers.abstract: Campylobacter is a constant concern in ensuring food safety, as it is one of the most common pathogens in food. The main source of Campylobacter species in food is poultry meat, and the primary production of this meat is a critical point where measures need to be taken to reduce its presence in the food chain. Therefore, poultry slaughterhouses are recognized as places where it is necessary to implement measures to control and reduce the number of Campylobacter spp. Food business operators are obliged to ensure greater hygiene on the slaughter line, through the inspection of equipment for each step of slaughter and the application of regular cleaning protocols. Continuous monitoring of the presence and abundance of Campylobacter spp. on the slaughter line provides data on the validity of hygiene control measures in the slaughterhouse, as well as the data needed to assess the microbiological risk in poultry meat. papers.title: ACCM-Net: an adaptive CLAHE-CBAM-MobileNet architecture for wheat leaf disease classification
papers.authors: V. S. S. Babu M, Sarat Kumar Kotamraju, Sri Kavya K. Ch.
papers.abstract: Wheat disease classification is critical for early detection and crop management, but manual identification is challenging due to visually similar symptoms in early infection stages. Existing deep learning approaches are not adept at addressing class imbalance, complex lesion patterns, and non-uniform field conditions, and thus, practical use is obstructed. To address this, this paper presents ACCM-Net, a fusion architecture founded on a frozen MobileNetV2 backbone and Convolutional Block Attention Module (CBAM) for enhanced feature refinement, combined with adaptive CLAHE and Sobel-based preprocessing to emphasize disease-discriminative regions. The model incorporates dynamic learning rate scheduling for stable training and enhanced generalization. Evaluated on a Kaggle-sourced dataset of 407 wheat leaf images, ACCM-Net attained an overall accuracy of 97.56%, F1-score of 97.60%, sensitivity of 98.41%, and specificity of 98.92%, beating baseline CNN and five other pre-trained models. papers.title: Compensatory abundance dynamics between an omnivore and a herbivore in agricultural landscapes
papers.authors: Takeshi Honda, Zhaowen Jiang
papers.abstract: Population ecology grew from a question about how competition governs animal abundance, and its classic models center on intraspecific competition, by which a population is regulated toward its own carrying capacity. But abundance also responds to competition between species. Where two species draw on a shared carrying capacity, density compensation can occur, a decline in one offset by an increase in another. Well documented within a guild, it has rarely been examined across guilds, for instance between a herbivore and an omnivore, whose diets are expected to be too distinct for their numbers to be coupled. Whether single‐population models should be extended to such cross‐guild regulation remains open. Here we report a pattern suggesting that such coupling may arise in agricultural landscapes. We tracked the ungulate community of one region in central Japan from 2006 to 2024 using two catch‐per‐unit‐effort indices, from trapping near farmland and from gun hunting in forest interiors. papers.authors: Cai Yihan, Ririko Koido, Nagai Chihiro, Hirota Mitsuru, 0000001397
papers.abstract: Wild boar (Sus scrofa) is one of the most widely distributed wild ungulates, and its populations are increasing and expanding globally due to socioeconomic change, reduced predator pressure, and climate warming. Rooting, a characteristic foraging behavior in which wild boars overturn litter, vegetation, and soil, is a major disturbance in forest ecosystems and can alter soil properties, biotic communities, ecosystem processes, and ecosystem services. In this literature review, we synthesize current knowledge of wild boar rooting in forest ecosystems. We first summarize the drivers of rooting regimes. We then review rooting-induced changes in soil physical and chemical properties, the community structure of soil microbes, invertebrates, and understory vegetation, as well as ecosystem processes and functions, including carbon and nitrogen dynamics and forest regeneration. We also discuss methodological challenges in quantifying rooting and their implications for cross-study comparisons. By reviewing previous studies, we found that both rooting regimes and their ecological impacts are highly context dependent. papers.title: Economic and Livelihood Impacts of Meteorological Disasters across Different Climatic Zones of Cameroon: A Mixed-methods Assessment
papers.authors: Mabel Nechia Wantim, Nchini Livinus Wayih, Mirabel Andin Ntali, Anyang Gordin Bah, Sambila Princewill
papers.source: OpenAlex / Journal of Geography Environment and Earth Science International
papers.abstract: Cameroon experiences recurrent meteorological disasters whose livelihood and economic consequences vary across its major climatic zones. This study assessed common meteorological disasters, their economic and livelihood impacts, and the adaptation strategies used by vulnerable populations in six cities representing four climatic zones. A mixed-methods design combined 1,200 household questionnaires administered in Douala, Tiko, and Bamenda with focus group discussions, key informant interviews, and field observations conducted in Yaoundé, Garoua, and Maroua. Findings showed that floods, landslides, and disease outbreaks were prominent in the Equatorial Cameroon and Equatorial Guinean climatic zones, whereas floods, droughts, dust storms, heatwaves, wildfires, and epidemics were frequently reported in the Sahelian zones. Overall, 65.9% of respondents reported that changing climatic conditions affected their livelihoods. papers.abstract: <jats:p>Background: Minimally invasive coronary artery bypass grafting (MICS CABG) via left anterior thoracotomy has emerged as a less invasive alternative to conventional open sternotomy (OPEN CABG), offering potential benefits in perioperative outcomes and complication rates. Objective. The aim of this study was to compare procedural characteristics, ventilation duration, drainage volumes, and postoperative complications between MICS CABG and OPEN CABG in a single-center cohort in Bosnia and Herzegovina. Methods. This retrospective cross-sectional study included 262 patients who underwent surgical revascularization between January 2019 and June 2023. Results. MICS CABG was associated with a shorter median procedure time (2.5 vs. 3.5 hours, p<0.001) and reduced mechanical ventilation duration (11.0 vs. 14.0 hours, p<0.001). Although ICU stay was similar (3.0 days, p=0.001), total hospitalization was shorter for MICS CABG (6.0 vs. 7.0 days, p<0.001). papers.abstract: Hypoxia is closely associated with tumor progression, metastasis, therapeutic resistance, and diagnostic challenges. The timely detection of hypoxia in live cancer cells is critical for early cancer diagnosis and for monitoring the effectiveness of anticancer therapies. Recently, there has been growing interest in non-covalent supramolecular design strategies for the development of hypoxia-sensitive sensors and prodrugs. Unlike the widely employed covalent approach, supramolecular chemistry eliminates the need for complex and time-consuming synthetic processes. Instead, the individual components of the sensor autonomously self-assemble into the desired structure. This review provides an overview of hypoxia-targeted and hypoxia-activated supramolecular probes, along with their mechanisms of action in tumor diagnosis and therapy. The supramolecular systems considered are classified according to the use of certain classes of macrocycles. The role of macrocyclic derivatives in the various proposed approaches and the response patterns of hypoxic targets will also be analyzed. papers.abstract: Psychomotor alterations may represent an important symptom dimension of major psychiatric disorders. Actigraphy enables the objective assessment of motor activity and rest–activity rhythms in naturalistic settings. The aim of this dissertation was to investigate psychomotor patterns associated with the schizophrenia and bipolar spectra using detailed actigraphic feature extraction and machine learning methods. The dissertation is based on two cross-sectional studies. In the first study, we examined the actigraphic profiles of individuals without a psychiatric diagnosis who were characterised by cyclothymic temperament (CFG) or positive schizotypal traits (PSF), compared with controls. In the second study, using two independent databases, we analysed the model patterns of the PSF group and individuals with chronic schizophrenia (CS), each relative to their respective control group. papers.title: Human-capital architecture for biosafety and responsible synthetic biology
papers.authors: Ibrokhim Yulchievich Abdurakhmonov
papers.source: OpenAlex / Frontiers in Bioengineering and Biotechnology
papers.abstract: Synthetic biology is entering practical use across medicine, agriculture, industrial biomanufacturing, food systems and environmental applications. This transition creates biosafety and biosecurity challenges that technical safeguards or compliance rules alone cannot solve. The recent UNESCO International Bioethics Committee (IBC) report provides an important ethical perimeter for synthetic biology, but principles must be translated into research habits, institutional cultures and deployment practices. This Perspective proposes a dual-framework model: the UNESCO IBC report defines boundary conditions for responsible biological innovation, while the Humanity, Ethics, Creativity and Imagination (HECI) framework strengthens the human capacities needed to work responsibly within them. Drawing on agricultural education and policy reform in Uzbekistan as a proof-of-principle, the article argues that biosafety in synthetic biology requires not only safer rules, but also scientists, institutions and regulators capable of empathy, judgment, creativity and foresight. Smith), has become the most damaging insect pest of maize in Pakistan since its 2019 incursion into Punjab, and commercial binary premixed insecticides have reached the market faster than locally generated efficacy data to support their use. This study evaluated the comparative bioefficacy of seven binary premixed insecticide formulations against a field-collected Sahiwal strain of S. frugiperda under laboratory and field conditions. In the laboratory, third-, fourth-, and fifth-instar larvae were exposed to five serial concentrations (0.25–4× the recommended field rate) using a leaf-dip bioassay in a completely randomized design, with mortality scored at 12, 24, 48, 72, and 168 hours. A parallel field trial assessed larval population and leaf-damage reduction at 3, 7, and 14 days after treatment. Both insecticide and concentration significantly affected mortality (p < .001 in nearly all cases), with concentration the dominant factor; mean 168-hour mortality of third-instar larvae rose from 22.7% at the lowest dose to 77.7% at the highest. papers.authors: Mary Fantasia, Aasma Sharma, Sudeep Bag, Paulo S. G. Cremonez, Clint A. Penick
papers.abstract: Whiteflies ( Bemisia tabaci ) are major agricultural pests causing over $100 million in losses to vegetable production annually through the transmission of plant viruses. Characterizing the virome of B. tabaci is critical for understanding vectoring potential and identifying candidate viral biocontrol agents. In this study, B. tabaci were collected from cucurbit crops in Tifton, Georgia, across two consecutive years, 2023 and 2024. Total RNA was extracted and ribodepleted, then sequenced with 150 bp paired-end reads on the Illumina NovaSeq 6000. Bioinformatics analyses included quality-assessing raw reads, which were trimmed prior to mapping to the B. tabaci reference genome (GCF_918797505.1) on the Alabama HPC, then mapping to a viral database (viral2019-03) using the Galaxy platform. After de novo transcriptome assembly using rnaviralSPAdes, the assembled contigs were screened for viral similarity using BLAST-based searches against the NCBI non-redundant nucleotide (nt) and non-redundant protein (nr) databases. papers.abstract: Abstract Fungicides are widely used in crop protection to control phytopathogenic fungi, yet their effects on non-target microorganisms inhabiting plant tissues remain poorly understood. Endophytic fungi are components of the plant microbiome, but assessing how fungicide applications influence their colonisation is challenging because these interactions are often asymptomatic. papers.abstract: Abstract Landscape structure shapes herbivorous insect distribution and abundance, yet its effects on scolytine beetles in exotic pine plantations remain poorly understood. We analysed patch‐scale (patch area, Euclidean nearest‐neighbour distance) and landscape‐scale (total core area of pine, mean nearest‐neighbour distance) metrics on the abundance of nine Scolytinae species in fragmented pine plantations of central Córdoba, Argentina. The analyses revealed contrasting responses structured by ecological guild. The pine‐specialist bark beetle Hylurgus ligniperda showed higher abundance in landscapes with greater connectivity (shorter mean inter‐patch distances), reflecting its long‐distance dispersal capacity. papers.title: Ruination conservation: Protecting life in Anthropocene ecosystems. Peñuelas Reserve, Chile
papers.authors: Tomás Undurraga, Tomás Ariztía, Mario Fergnani
papers.source: OpenAlex / Environment and Planning E Nature and Space
papers.abstract: This article introduces the concept of ruination conservation to analyze how environmental protection is enacted in novel ecosystems under conditions of damage, hybridity, and institutional precarity in the Anthropocene. Moving beyond conservation models that seek to restore pristine nature, we examine conservation as a situated practice oriented toward sustaining life in irreversibly altered landscapes. Drawing on a deep qualitative research conducted in the Lago Peñuelas National Reserve in central Chile between 2023 and 2026—including 15 ethnographic fieldwork visits, 21 in-depth interviews, and documentary analysis—we conceptualize conservation as a form of socio-ecological care shaped by historical interventions, infrastructural decay, and competing land uses. We identify three defining features of ruination conservation. First, it entails the acceptance of ecological impurity, where native and exotic species, as well as hybrid forms of life, coexist within degraded environments. papers.authors: Yun Xing, Fengxu Chen, Gonggeng Liu, Shijun Bao, Xujian Zhang
papers.abstract: The widespread proliferation of electromagnetic technologies in communications, healthcare, and daily life poses increasing risks of radiation-induced tissue injury. Mitigating these deleterious effects remains a formidable challenge. Recently, medical gases, including molecular hydrogen (H2), hydrogen sulfide (H2S), carbon monoxide (CO), nitric oxide (NO), and hyperbaric oxygen, have emerged as a promising therapeutic modality with radioprotective potential. These gases exert their effects through integrated, anti-inflammatory, anti-apoptotic, and mitochondrial-protective mechanisms. Specifically, the endogenous gasotransmitters (CO, NO, and H2S) modulate precise signaling networks, while the exogenous interventions (H2, and hyperbaric oxygen) function primarily through direct radical scavenging or the induction of hormetic stress responses. This review evaluates the research progress of these five medical gases in preventing and treating injuries across the electromagnetic spectrum. H2 possesses the broadest evidence base, particularly in radiofrequency and ultraviolet protection. H2S and CO demonstrate potent efficacy in addressing ultraviolet-induced skin and retinal damage. papers.authors: Kumar Anil, Bhupendra Koul, K Subhash
papers.abstract: Vegetables are the major food source for nutritional security for the teeming millions across the globe. Unfortunately, the growth and development of vegetable crops face yield reduction due to the infestation of notorious sedentary endoparasites, root-knot nematodes (RKN, Meloidogyne spp.). The RKN substantially harm the vegetable crops (20–100 %) culminating in huge economic losses to the growers, becoming a serious threat to the world agricultural sector. Chemical-based nematicides are effective to a certain extent but are costly, unsafe for humans and animals and subject to various regulations. Hence, it is crucial to use green and sustainable approaches for managing RKN infection. Approaches such as cultural practices, application of cover/antagonistic crops, use of organic amendments, nanoparticles (NPs) and chemical nematicides have been deployed for management of RKN. However, application of biocontrol agents is a safer, more reliable, cost-effective and promising alternative method for management of RKN. One such factor, human-animal contact, remains poorly understood. papers.title: Before Qualia, Strategic Existence Begins

papers.abstract: Before evolution can select anything, a physically possible causal architecture must already exist for selection to exploit. The T4 bacteriophage, a mindless nanoscale machine whose structure executes functions that map onto both empowering and disempowering strategies in Forde's framework of social dynamics, demonstrates this principle at the nanoscale. The strategies mapped include security, knowledge, hope, fairness, unity, and dignity, alongside their darker counterparts: nativism, hierarchy, misinformation, subjugation, dehumanization, and fear. Each concept is paired with a specific biological mechanism, virion stability, irreversible adsorption, superinfection exclusion, among others, showing that the mapping is grounded in observable structure. These mappings do not reify nonhuman organisms or attribute human qualities to mindless machines. They are structural descriptions: the concepts name functions that the architecture performs, not feelings that the organism experiences. Concerns regarding long-term graft survival, infection, and urological morbidity persist, yet adult-specific outcome synthesis and clinically useful guidance are lacking. Methods: We performed a Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses-compliant systematic review of studies reporting posttransplant outcomes in adults with abnormal or surgically MLUT anatomy. Results: Twenty-four studies, including 511 MLUT recipients, were identified. Most were retrospective single-center series, and only a minority included comparator cohorts. Several studies included mixed adult-pediatric cohorts where adult-only outcomes could not be separated. papers.abstract: Genetically modified phosphate-solubilizing bacteria (PSB) lack systematic feedback integration among four dimensions — gene-target selection(D1), engineering-strategy design (D2), field performance (D3) and environmental-safety constraints (D4) — giving rise to a fundamental dilemma across the research field. The central thesis is that the field’s current bottleneck is not a technical deficiency in any single dimension, but rather a disconnect between dimensions: misalignment between target identification and engineering strategy, between engineering design and agronomic performance, and between safety assessment and the full product development pipeline. papers.authors: Chunhong Li, Kejiang Chen, Yijia Xia, Siling Li, Keda Jiang
papers.abstract: Green mold caused by Penicillium digitatum severely limits the postharvest storage of lemon fruit. β-Aminobutyric acid (BABA) is known to enhance disease resistance in harvested fruit, but the transcriptional basis by which BABA reinforces defense responses in infected lemon peel remains insufficiently understood. Here, BABA pretreatment slowed the development of green mold in postharvest lemon fruit, as reflected by smaller lesions, reduced fungal biomass, and less infection-associated tissue damage. RNA-seq analysis showed that BABA did not merely intensify the overall response to P. digitatum , but reshaped a defined subset of pathogen-responsive genes. Among the enriched pathways, phenylpropanoid biosynthesis was particularly prominent, with lignin biosynthesis-related genes showing stronger induction in BABA-pretreated infected fruit than in fruit inoculated with the pathogen alone. Consistently, BABA pretreatment increased lignin accumulation and enhanced phloroglucinol-HCl staining around inoculation sites. papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Industrial poultry technologies and processes are reshaping the knowledge, practice and agrobiodiversity of criollo ( Gallus domesticus ) or backyard hen keeping, as well as outcompeting this livelihood in formal markets. This transition undermines women's autonomy and socio‐economic resilience by engendering dependence on market inputs, including imported poultry, pharmaceutical inputs and feed. Despite the accelerated expansion of the industrial poultry sector in Colombia, criollo hen keeping persists for subsistence and informal markets. This paper asks why and how criollo hen keeping persists and how women differentially resist the industrial poultry sector and intersecting gendered power dynamics through everyday practices of care. The paper draws on a subset of nine semistructured interviews from two projects working across several regions in Colombia, which both employed participative research action and co‐produced methods. papers.title: ArthroVerse: mapping protein family diversity across arthropod-associated microbiomes
papers.authors: Iro N Chasapi, Eleni Aplakidou, Maria N Chasapi, Efthimia Lamari, Αλέξανδρος Γαλάρας
papers.abstract: Metagenomic studies of arthropod-associated microbiomes have generated vast amounts of sequence data, yet the functional and structural organization of these proteins remains largely unexplored. Here, we present ArthroVerse, the first comprehensive database of protein families derived from arthropod-associated metagenomes. Non-redundant protein families were generated after rigorous filtering, deduplication, and clustering. The protein families were further annotated with microbial taxonomy, host associations, protein structural information, and carbohydrate-active enzymes predictions. The resulting dataset integrates both metagenomic and reference genome-derived proteins, enabling systematic exploration of functional diversity, evolutionary relationships, and host-microbe interactions in insect microbiomes. ArthroVerse provides a valuable resource for the study of microbial ecology and arthropod physiology, offering unprecedented insight into the protein landscape of insect-associated microbial communities. ArthroVerse is publicly accessible at https://envofams.org/arthroverse/.

papers.authors: Kyle Davis, Joanna Tannous
